newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Japanese Catholic bishop among Malaysian detainees.
newsitem.headline: Japanese Catholic bishop among Malaysian detainees.

text.p: Two Roman Catholic bishops were among nearly 40 foreign participants detained on Saturday by Malaysian police at a controversial conference on East Timor, witnesses and conference organisers said.

The Rev. Aloisuis Nobulo Somo of Japan and the Rev. Hilton Deakin of Melbourne, Australia, were taken along with the other foreign participants in a police truck to the Malaysian Immigration Department, witnesses said.
Bishop Aloisuis celebrated the Catholic Mass in 1993 in the East Timor capital of Dili with Bishop Carlos Belo, last month's co-winner of the Nobel peace prize, conference organisers said.

The 36 foreigners were herded onto a police truck with their luggage after being escorted out of a central Kuala Lumpur hotel, witnesses said. Conference organisers said they expected the foreigners would most likely be deported.

The bishops and other foreigners were in Kuala Lumpur to attend the Asia Pacific Conference on East Timor, which was broken up on Saturday by a youth group allied to Malayian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad's ruling coalition.

The Malaysian government had earlier banned the meeting, saying it could harm ties with neighbouring Indonesia, which invaded the former Portuguese colony of East Timor in 1975 and annexed it the following year.
